title: Minimum Increase to Maximize Special Indices
summary: Given an integer array nums, find the minimum number of operations needed to make as many indices as possible special, where an index is special if the element at that index is greater than its neighbors.
statement: Given an integer array nums, find the minimum number of operations needed to make as many indices as possible special, where an index is special if the element at that index is greater than its neighbors. Each operation consists of increasing any element by one.
constraints: nums is a nonempty integer array.
Only interior indices may be peaks; an operation increases one element by one.
First maximize the number of peaks, then return the minimum operations needed to attain that maximum.
hints: A maximum set of interior peaks uses alternating indices; even lengths allow one parity shift.
Compute the independent cost of raising each candidate above its two original neighbors.
A two-state suffix DP either follows the current parity or spends the one allowed skip before continuing.
Adjacent peaks are impossible, and maximum cardinality leaves at most one extra gap; the DP enumerates exactly those layouts and minimizes their additive costs.
editorial: Adjacent peaks are impossible, and maximum cardinality leaves at most one extra gap; the DP enumerates exactly those layouts and minimizes their additive costs.

tests.explanation: Only index one can be a peak; increasing it once makes 3>1 and 3>2.
The middle is already a peak, so zero operations are needed.
